issue.title: Pid-recycling-guard commit broke 11 tests: unexpected process_identity key + pid-based filtering regressions
issue.description:
## Discovered while verifying an unrelated modals/__init__.py file-split task

On 2026-08-27, `just check-full` on master (tree at/near a646bdaf6, which includes
"fix(agent): guard runner slots against pid recycling") failed 11 tests that are
unrelated to the modals split in progress. Confirmed unrelated by stashing the modals
diff (`src/sase/ace/tui/modals/__init__.py` + new `_export_table.py`) and re-running:
all 11 fail identically on a clean tree with no modals changes present.

Likely root cause: the pid-recycling-guard commit appears to have changed
process/agent-identity tracking (a new `process_identity` key shows up in written
`agent_meta.json`, and pid-based matching/filtering logic elsewhere behaves
differently), and several tests were not updated for the new shape/behavior.

### Confirmed reproducible in isolation (ran directly with pytest, no full suite needed)

- `tests/axe/test_agent_meta_atomic.py::test_generic_and_specialized_agent_meta_writers_use_atomic_publication`
  — asserts the specialized-writer's `agent_meta.json` equals a fixed dict with keys
  `pid, model, llm_provider, vcs_provider, tribe`; the actual dict now also contains an
  unexpected `process_identity` key (e.g. `"1813a6cb-0636-4d82-abd0-e497532b3a99:17"`).
  This is the clearest smoking gun for the new/changed field.
- `tests/test_agent_wait_cli.py::test_all_excludes_caller_and_its_family` — expects
  `payload["targets"]` names to equal `["good"]`, gets `[]`. pid-based
  caller/family-exclusion filtering appears broken.
- `tests/test_agent_wait_cli.py::test_exit_code_timeout` — `assert 3 == 4`.
- `tests/test_agent_wait_live.py::test_why_column_for_waiting_queued_monitor_and_prompt`
- `tests/test_agent_wait_live.py::test_terminal_blocker_warning_when_dependency_failed`
- `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_list_running_agents_filters_done_and_dead`
- `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_list_running_agents_surfaces_slot_relevant_parallel_children`
- `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_running_listing_slot_occupancy_matches_admission_count`
- `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_list_running_agents_reports_waiting_marker`
- `tests/test_running_agents_snapshot.py::test_list_all_agents_includes_done_and_failed`
- `tests/test_agent_chat_from_name.py::test_explicit_running_agent_falls_back_to_meta_chat_path`

All 11 were run together via a single `pytest` invocation (no `-p xdist`, no full
suite) and failed the same way both with and without the modals diff present, so this
is not full-parallel-lane leakage — it is a deterministic regression on current master.

### Possibly related, needs separate confirmation

- `tests/fakey/test_runner_slots_e2e.py::test_fakey_agents_respect_cap_and_release_in_fifo_order`
  — timed out waiting for `slot-2` to start (`_WAIT_TIMEOUT` exceeded) when run in a
  small isolated pytest invocation together with only its sibling test (not the full
  suite), so this doesn't look like ordinary full-lane resource contention either. Given
  it's in the same runner-slots subsystem the pid-recycling-guard commit touched, it may
  share the same root cause as the 11 above, but it's a timeout rather than a clean
  assertion mismatch, so treat it as a separate lead to confirm rather than assumed same
  bug. (Its sibling `test_child_is_exempt_while_repeat_roots_stay_capped` is already
  tracked separately as sase-n6, which this run also reproduced and was +1'd there.)

### Why this is not a flake

The 11 confirmed nodes above fail every time, in a small non-full-suite pytest
invocation, both immediately after each other and reproduced identically with the
unrelated modals-split diff stashed out. This is a deterministic true failure on
master, not full-parallel-lane state leakage.

### Scope

Bisect/inspect the pid-recycling-guard change (commit subject: "fix(agent): guard
runner slots against pid recycling", near a646bdaf6) for the new `process_identity`
field and any changed pid-based filtering/matching logic, then decide per test whether
the test's expectation is stale (update it) or the runtime behavior regressed (fix it).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Reproduced deterministically in a small isolated pytest invocation (not the full suite), both with and without an unrelated modals-split diff present; the same 11 nodes fail identically every time on current master, so this is a true regression, not full-parallel-lane leakage.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction while verifying test_artifacts_relation_collapse split on 2026-08-27. just check escalated to the full suite after the linked core checkout fast-forwarded and failed eight nodes; reran the failing areas serial with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q and reproduced the agent-family failures deterministically: test_live_failed_plan_family_projects_retry_immediately had no plan agent, test_pid_dedup_preserves_followup_workflow_agents returned 2 agents instead of 3, and four test_agent_loader_epic_created_status nodes missed EPIC APPROVED/planner projections. The pager rail nodes from the full-suite failure passed in the focused rerun, so this corroboration is limited to the agent loader/projection regression.

Independent reproduction while implementing gate_handoff_outcome_parity on 2026-08-27. Focused gate-handoff tests passed, but just check escalated to the full suite after src/sase/core/dismissed_agent_completion.py changed and failed eight nodes. Rerunning the failed node IDs serial reproduced the same deterministic agent-loader/projection cluster: test_live_failed_plan_family_projects_retry_immediately had no planner child, test_pid_dedup_preserves_followup_workflow_agents returned 2 rows instead of 3, and four test_agent_loader_epic_created_status nodes missed EPIC APPROVED / synthetic planner projection. The two pager rail nodes from the full-suite failure passed in the focused rerun, so this +1 is limited to the agent-loader/projection regression.

Independent reproduction recorded by proposing phase sase-ud.13.1.3.1.1 note 1 on master a646bdaf6: the same 11 process_identity/pid-filtering nodes failed deterministically in isolation and blocked the phase just check. The exact affected modules pass on current master (72-test focused rerun), so this corroborates the historical regression and impact without claiming it still reproduces.

payload.description: The same master window introduced pid/process-identity runner-slot regressions; inspect for a shared cause without assuming semantic duplication.
Same process_identity/pid-filtering seam: a worker changing how planted PIDs are judged alive will touch the tests sase-uw reports broken by the pid-recycling guard.
